description: This topic covers the simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous forms of the present, past and future tenses, together with regular and irregular verbs, subject-verb agreement and common tense errors.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb form: 'Every morning, Juma _____ his cattle to the river.'
mcq.explanation: The present simple is used for habitual actions, and a singular third-person subject like 'Juma' takes the verb ending in -s.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence is in the present continuous tense?

options.text: The pupils have sung the anthem.

mcq.explanation: The present continuous is formed with 'am/is/are' plus the -ing form and describes an action happening at the moment of speaking.

mcq.questionText: What is the correct past tense of the irregular verb 'bring'?
mcq.explanation: 'Bring' is an irregular verb whose past simple and past participle are both 'brought'.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct sentence in the future simple tense.

options.text: We will visit our grandmother next week.
We visiting our grandmother next week.
We visited our grandmother next week.
We have visit our grandmother next week.

mcq.explanation: The future simple is formed with 'will' plus the base form of the verb to express an action that has not yet happened.

mcq.questionText: Select the correct verb: 'My sisters _____ to the market every Saturday.'
mcq.explanation: A plural subject ('My sisters') takes the base form of the verb without -s in the present simple tense.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect tense?

options.text: She has finished her homework already.
She finished her homework already have.
She have finish her homework already.

mcq.explanation: The present perfect is formed with 'has/have' plus the past participle and often shows a recently completed action linked to the present.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb form: 'While the rain _____, the children were playing inside.'
mcq.explanation: The past continuous ('was falling') describes an action in progress in the past that was happening at the same time as another past action.

options.text: Neither the teacher nor the pupils was present.
Neither the teacher nor the pupils were present.
Neither the teacher nor the pupils is present.
Neither the teacher nor the pupils been present.

mcq.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject; here 'pupils' is plural, so 'were' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Identify the tense in this sentence: 'By the time the bus arrived, we had bought our tickets.'
mcq.explanation: The past perfect ('had bought') shows an action completed before another past action ('the bus arrived').

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb form: 'The water in the tank _____ very low this week.'
mcq.explanation: 'Water' is an uncountable noun treated as singular, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the future continuous tense?

options.text: At noon tomorrow, I will be writing my examination.
At noon tomorrow, I will written my examination.
At noon tomorrow, I am writing my examination.
At noon tomorrow, I have been writing my examination.

mcq.explanation: The future continuous ('will be writing') describes an action that will be in progress at a specific future time.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb form: 'Each of the boys _____ a clean uniform today.'
mcq.explanation: 'Each' is singular and always takes a singular verb, so 'wears' is correct regardless of the plural noun that follows.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect continuous tense?

options.text: Halima has been studying since morning.
Halima have been study since morning.
Halima is been studying since morning.

mcq.explanation: The present perfect continuous is formed with 'has/have been' plus the -ing form and emphasises an action that began in the past and continues now.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb form: 'If he _____ harder last term, he would have passed the test.'
mcq.explanation: In a third conditional referring to an unreal past, the 'if' clause uses the past perfect ('had studied').

mcq.questionText: Which sentence shows correct subject-verb agreement?

options.text: The news about the floods were shocking.
The news about the floods was shocking.
The news about the floods are shocking.
The news about the floods have shocking.

mcq.explanation: 'News' is a singular uncountable noun and takes a singular verb, so 'was' is correct.

fib.questionText: The sun _____ in the east every day. (rise)
fib.explanation: A general truth uses the present simple, and the singular subject 'sun' takes the verb ending in -s.

fib.questionText: Yesterday the farmers _____ their seeds before the rain came. (plant)
fib.explanation: 'Plant' is a regular verb, so its past simple is formed by adding -ed.

fib.questionText: Look! The baby _____ at the colourful kite. (point)
fib.explanation: The present continuous ('is pointing') is used for an action happening right now, often signalled by 'Look!'.

fib.questionText: Next month we _____ a new computer for the school library. (buy)
fib.explanation: The future simple uses 'will' plus the base form of the verb for a planned future action.

fib.questionText: She has already _____ the letter to her cousin. (write)
fib.explanation: After 'has' the present perfect requires the past participle, and the irregular verb 'write' becomes 'written'.

fib.questionText: While I was cooking, my brother _____ the floor. (sweep)
fib.explanation: Two actions in progress at the same time in the past use the past continuous form.

fib.questionText: The pupils _____ their classroom before the inspector arrived. (clean)
fib.explanation: The past perfect ('had cleaned') shows the cleaning was completed before another past event.

fib.questionText: My grandfather _____ in this village since 1980. (live)
fib.explanation: The present perfect with 'since' shows an action that began in the past and continues to the present.

fib.questionText: By next year, my father _____ this house for ten years. (own)
fib.explanation: The future perfect ('will have owned') describes an action that will be completed by a point in the future.

fib.questionText: They _____ for the bus for two hours when it finally appeared. (wait)
fib.explanation: The past perfect continuous ('had been waiting') emphasises the duration of an ongoing action before another past event.

tf.questionText: The present simple tense is used to describe actions that happen regularly or habitually.
tf.explanation: The present simple expresses habits, routines and general truths, such as 'I walk to school'.

tf.questionText: The past tense of the regular verb 'jump' is 'jumpt'.
tf.explanation: Regular verbs form the past simple by adding -ed, so the correct form is 'jumped'.

tf.questionText: The verb 'go' is an irregular verb whose past simple form is 'went'.
tf.explanation: 'Go' does not follow the -ed rule; its past simple is 'went' and its past participle is 'gone'.

tf.questionText: The present continuous tense is formed using 'am', 'is' or 'are' together with the -ing form of the verb.
tf.explanation: For example, 'They are reading' uses 'are' plus the -ing form to show an action in progress.

tf.questionText: A singular subject in the present simple always takes a verb without the -s ending.
tf.explanation: A singular third-person subject takes the -s ending, as in 'He runs', so the statement is false.

tf.questionText: The present perfect tense is formed with 'has' or 'have' plus the past participle of the verb.
tf.explanation: For example, 'She has eaten' combines 'has' with the past participle 'eaten'.

tf.questionText: In the sentence 'The team are playing well', the word 'team' must always take a plural verb.
tf.explanation: Collective nouns like 'team' can take a singular or plural verb depending on whether they are seen as one unit or as individuals.

tf.questionText: The past perfect tense is used to show that one past action happened before another past action.
tf.explanation: For example, 'She had left before I arrived' shows the leaving came before the arriving.

tf.questionText: The sentence 'He don't like tea' uses correct subject-verb agreement.
tf.explanation: A singular subject like 'He' requires 'does not' (doesn't), so the correct form is 'He doesn't like tea'.

tf.questionText: The future perfect continuous tense uses 'will have been' plus the -ing form of the verb.
tf.explanation: For example, 'By June she will have been teaching for five years' uses 'will have been' plus 'teaching'.

summary.questionText: How is the present simple tense mainly used?
summary.correctAnswer: For habits, routines and general truths.
summary.explanation: Example: 'Birds fly south in the dry season.'

summary.questionText: How is the present continuous tense formed?
summary.correctAnswer: am/is/are plus the -ing form of the verb.
summary.explanation: It describes an action happening at the moment of speaking.

summary.questionText: How do regular verbs form their past simple tense?
summary.correctAnswer: By adding -ed to the base verb.

summary.questionText: What is special about irregular verbs in the past tense?
summary.correctAnswer: They do not add -ed; they change form.

summary.questionText: How is the future simple tense formed?
summary.correctAnswer: will plus the base form of the verb.

summary.questionText: How is the present perfect tense formed?
What does the past perfect tense show?
summary.correctAnswer: An action completed before another past action.
summary.explanation: It is formed with 'had' plus the past participle.

summary.correctAnswer: The verb must match its subject in number.
summary.explanation: A singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb.

summary.questionText: What verb form follows a third-person singular subject in the present simple?
summary.correctAnswer: The verb takes an -s or -es ending.

summary.questionText: What does the present perfect continuous tense emphasise?
summary.correctAnswer: The duration of an action continuing into the present.
summary.explanation: It is formed with 'has/have been' plus the -ing form, as in 'I have been reading'.

hoq.questionText: Read the sentence and choose the option that corrects all the tense errors: 'When I reached home yesterday, my mother already cook the meal and my father is resting.'

options.text: When I reached home yesterday, my mother had already cooked the meal and my father was resting.
When I reach home yesterday, my mother already cooked the meal and my father is resting.
When I reached home yesterday, my mother has already cooked the meal and my father is resting.
When I reached home yesterday, my mother already cooks the meal and my father rests.

hoq.explanation: The cooking was completed before the arrival, so it needs the past perfect ('had cooked'), and the action in progress at that past time needs the past continuous ('was resting').

hoq.questionText: Choose the sentence in which every verb correctly agrees with its subject.

options.text: Each of the students who attends the club bring a notebook and writes notes.
Each of the students who attend the club brings a notebook and writes notes.
Each of the students who attend the club bring a notebook and write notes.
Each of the students who attends the club brings a notebook and write notes.

hoq.explanation: 'Each' is singular and governs 'brings' and 'writes', while the relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural 'students' and takes 'attend'.

hoq.questionText: Which sentence correctly combines the ideas using the future perfect tense?

options.text: By the time the guests arrive, we will finish decorating the hall.
By the time the guests arrive, we will have finished decorating the hall.
By the time the guests arrive, we have finished decorating the hall.
By the time the guests arrive, we are finishing decorating the hall.

hoq.explanation: The future perfect ('will have finished') shows that the decorating will be complete before the future moment when the guests arrive.
